extracted.intended_audience: MathML authors, web developers, and assistive-technology (AT) implementors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for annotating MathML expressions (intent, semantics, annotation, annotation-xml, parallel markup, tables/matrices and mixing presentation/content) to produce unambiguous, AT-friendly renderings and interoperable markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intent to disambiguate readings
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary use for intent is to disambiguate cases where the same syntax is used for different meanings, and typically has different readings (e.g., msup can mean power, transpose, derivative, or embellished symbol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate constructs with intent strings (examples: intent="power($base,$exp)", intent="$op($a)", intent=":postfix ($a)", intent="derivative($a)") so AT can produce the correct narration. Show readings with and without intent. Use underscore function (literal names) to give custom accessible names compositionally (e.g. intent="_x-new" or compound intents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer properties/core properties for tabular constructs; use intent only when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a kind of tabular construct has an associated property, it is usually better to use only the property and allow AT to infer how to speak and navigate the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use core properties so AT can generate appropriate speech (e.g., aligned equations vs matrix). When core properties are insufficient for complex layouts, use intent concept names and, if appropriate, properties from the open list. Because of likely complexity, testing with AT should be done to verify the voiced output matches author intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on CSS for accessible readouts; use intent for stylistic meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: CSS customization of MathML is generally not made available to AT and is ignored in accessible readouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors need meaningful stylistic emphasis (e.g., color-coding steps), annotate with intent (example: intent="highlighted-step($step)") so AT can express the emphasis (e.g., 'highlighted step of six over two').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive use of literal names not in dictionaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Literals are not in dictionaries; excessive use makes the meaning opaque and limits AT adaptability, translation and locale-specific speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage overuse of literal names; prefer named concepts in dictionaries when possible. When specific speech is needed, use literal names sparingly and with awareness they may limit AT behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use literal names (prefixed with _) rather than unsupported concept names for required specific speech
rubrics_metrics.description: When specific speech not corresponding to a meaningful concept is nevertheless required, it is better to use a literal name (prefixed with _) rather than an unsupported concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids unexpected collisions with future updates to concept dictionaries. Example: intent="_x-new" or composing fragments as intents for localized names (Cyrillic examples shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: semantics element structure and processor responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The semantics element is the container for an expression and its annotations; it contains the expression as its first child followed by zero or more annotation and/or annotation-xml elements. The semantics element is considered both a presentation and a content element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All MathML processors should process the semantics element even if they only process presentation or only content subsets. The default rendering of semantics is the default rendering of its first child. A renderer may use annotations to customize rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify annotation keys (cd/name or definitionURL); default key is alternate-representation
rubrics_metrics.description: An annotation key specifies the relationship between an expression and an annotation and is primary for a processor to decide whether to process an annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define annotation keys using cd and name attributes (or definitionURL). Processors are encouraged to examine both the annotation key and the encoding attribute to determine processability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alternate-representation for alternate renderings
rubrics_metrics.description: The alternate-representation annotation key specifies that the annotation value provides an alternate representation for an expression (often rendering hints), and generally does not alter meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label presentation MathML annotations with appropriate encoding (e.g., application/mathml-presentation+xml or MathML-Presentation) to indicate preferred rendering. When a presentation MathML annotation is present in semantics it may be used as the default rendering instead of the first child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contentequiv for semantically equivalent content (cannot be ignored)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contentequiv annotation key specifies that the annotation value provides a semantically equivalent alternative for the annotated expression and cannot be ignored without potentially changing behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use encoding="application/mathml-content+xml" (or MathML-Content) for content-equivalent annotations that disambiguate ambiguous presentation markup. Use contentequiv to make explicit that the annotation is a definitive content markup equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use encoding attribute to indicate annotation data format
rubrics_metrics.description: The encoding attribute indicates the data format (media type or self-describing string) of the annotation value and helps processors determine understandability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefined encoding values include MathML, MathML-Presentation, and MathML-Content. For external/other formats provide a clear encoding (e.g., application/x-maple, application/vnd.wolfram.mathematica, application/x-tex, application/openmath+xml) so processors can choose how to handle the annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use annotation references (src + encoding) for external annotations and processors should expand them
rubrics_metrics.description: A semantics element may contain empty annotation or annotation-xml elements that provide encoding and src attributes to specify external locations for the annotation value (annotation reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing agents that anticipate consumers may not be able to retrieve external entities should request the external content and replace the annotation with its expanded form. Annotation references follow the same rules to determine the annotation key.

rubrics_metrics.name: annotation element usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The annotation element is the container for a semantic annotation represented as parsed character data in a non-XML format; it should contain character data and must not contain XML markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If annotation contains XML reserved characters (&, <) they must be escaped or enclosed in CDATA (XML syntax). Attributes: definitionURL (URI), encoding (string), cd (content dictionary, default mathmlkeys), name (annotation key name, default alternate-representation), src (external location). The annotation element is semantic-mapping and may only be a child of semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: annotation-xml element usage rules and HTML parsing caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: The annotation-xml element contains structured XML markup as an annotation value and uses attributes similar to annotation (definitionURL, encoding, cd, name, src).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When MathML is parsed as HTML, namespace extensibility may not be available: xmlns attributes are treated as ordinary attributes and colon-prefixed element names are not treated as namespaced. If encoding is text/html or application/xhtml+xml the content is parsed as HTML; otherwise it is parsed as foreign content placed in the MathML namespace. Use of other vocabularies (OpenMath, RDF/XML) in HTML is considered invalid; avoid namespace prefixes and element names containing ':' in HTML. Prefer encoding annotations using existing vocabularies (Strict Content MathML, RDFa, etc.) when HTML validity matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraints for mixing presentation and content markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation markup encodes notational structure; content markup encodes functional structure. Embedding is allowed only under constraints to keep unambiguous structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation markup may appear in content markup only within ci and cn token elements, within csymbol, or within semantics. Content markup may be embedded within presentation markup only if each content fragment has an unambiguous presentation replacement and the resulting presentation expression is well-formed. The following content elements must not appear as immediate children of a presentation element: annotation, annotation-xml, bvar, condition, degree, logbase, lowlimit, uplimit. Content markup may not appear within presentation token elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel markup via semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel markup combines two or more markup trees for the same expression using the semantics element, enabling both presentation and content information to be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel markup may appear on its own or as part of a larger tree. A single semantics element may pair a presentation tree and a content tree (or vice versa). This facilitates applications that use both presentation and content information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use id and xref for cross-references in parallel markup; placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To support sub-expression selection in parallel markup, cross-references between branches of a semantics element are established using id and xref attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: id attributes referenced by any xref should be in the same branch of the enclosing semantics element to avoid cycles. It's often useful to place id attributes on the branch with the finest-grained node structure so other branches can xref subsets. In absence of other criteria, the first branch is a sensible choice to contain id attributes. The direction of references does not imply selection is limited to one child; selecting a subtree in any branch and recovering corresponding subtrees is feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix and system-of-equations intent usage and narration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: mtable and related constructs are used for matrices, systems of equations, proof-derivation steps, and for forced line breaking/alignment; their use affects how AT speaks and navigates the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a tabular construct has an associated property, prefer the property to enable AT to speak as a list of aligned equations rather than a matrix. For matrices and systems use intent markers (examples: intent='$m' with mtable intent=':matrix' or intent=':system-of-equations') to indicate structure; AT narration examples are shown (e.g., 'The 2 by 2 matrix; column 1; 1; column 2; 0; ... end matrix'). For wrapped/continued rows use row intents (':continued-row'). Test outputs with AT.
